The judgement layer

Fast output is useful. Accountable judgement is what makes it operational.

SNAXK asks a quieter set of questions before an agent continues: what changed, how much confidence is justified, which boundary applies, and what evidence must remain visible afterwards?

01 · signal

Notice meaning before momentum.

02 · consequence

Understand what this action could change.

03 · uncertainty

Slow down when confidence and consequence do not match.

Concept model

A loop that can pause itself.

Each move leaves a trail. Routine work can continue. Meaningful uncertainty reaches a boundary, and consequential work returns to review.

Five deliberate moves

Signal, meaning, boundary, reflection, review.

The loop is intentionally smaller than the systems around it. Its job is to help people inspect why an agent continued, paused, escalated, or changed course.

01

Fast heuristic pass

Scan messages, events, and signals before action. The first pass asks whether anything meaningful is happening.

02

Meaning check

Separate routine noise from work that is risky, surprising, sensitive, valuable, or likely to affect a human.

03

Bounded route

Triggered cases move through judgement boundaries: slow down, stop, escalate, adapt, or ask for human review.

04

Reflect overnight

The system does not carry every reaction forward. It reflects, compares, and waits before changing behaviour.

05

Reviewed carry-forward

Only changes that survive review become part of the agent's future judgement.

Stop lines

A boundary should be visible before it is crossed.

Permissions, privacy, safety, spending, publishing and accountability are not exceptions to tidy up later. They are part of the route.

  • 01
    When to slow down

    High consequence, weak evidence, unfamiliar context, or mismatched confidence.

  • 02
    When to stop

    A request crosses permission, privacy, safety, spending, publishing, or accountability boundaries.

  • 03
    What to share

    Judgement includes deciding what is appropriate to reveal, quote, remember, or pass to another system.

  • 04
    How to adapt

    The same action may be right for one person, wrong for another, and unclear until the context is reviewed.

Chief Agentic Officer

The board needs to inspect the judgement, not just the output.

A Chief Agentic Officer needs a clear view of what agentic work exists, who owns it, which boundaries apply, how uncertainty escalates, and what evidence survives after the work is done.
